subject: Decision framing: VPC/on-prem acceptance criteria and action lanes
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, procurement@blueharbor.com
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Decision framing: VPC/on-prem acceptance criteria and action lanes

Team / BlueHarbor procurement —

Thanks for the call this morning. We promised to capture a crisp decision frame so BlueHarbor can sign off on next steps. Attached is a draft acceptance criteria doc (vpc-acceptance-draft.pdf) and a high-level cost sketch (cost-estimate-rough.xlsx).

What I need from this thread by end of week:
- Product/arch: a checklist of technical acceptance criteria we must meet for a private VPC or on-prem pilot (network, latency/SLA, data residency, audit logs).
- Security/compliance: a minimal evidence list BlueHarbor will accept (SOC2 artifacts, network diagrams, KMS proof).
- Ops/resourcing: who owns the pilot on our side (eng lead, integration PM, SRE on-call) and an estimate of required FTE-weeks to stand up a pilot in a single region.
- Commercial: proposed gating milestones that trigger invoicing / committed capacity.

BlueHarbor: please confirm the target pilot timeline (they said "Q3 window") and any non-negotiable constraints (e.g., isolation of audit logs from other customers).

I put suggested owners inline in the attachment. Quick replies are fine — this is intentionally a tight framing exercise.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: vpc-acceptance-draft.pdf (application/pdf) — draft acceptance checklist
Attachment: cost-estimate-rough.xlsx (spreadsheet) — ballpark effort/cost

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision framing: VPC/on-prem acceptance criteria and action lanes

On Wed, May 30, 2028 at 09:14 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team / BlueHarbor procurement —
> 
> Thanks for the call this morning. We promised to capture a crisp decision frame so BlueHarbor can sign off on next steps. Attached is a draft acceptance criteria doc (vpc-acceptance-draft.pdf) and a high-level cost sketch (cost-estimate-rough.xlsx).

Thanks, Hannah — good start. A few architecture clarifications I think must be explicit in the acceptance criteria:

1) Minimum throughput and concurrency targets: quantify tokens/sec per shard and end-to-end P99 latency for 512-token prompts. BlueHarbor reported a peak of ~120 concurrent sessions in their demo; we should propose a pilot target (e.g., sustain 80 concurrent with P99 < 400ms).
2) KV cache persistence: if customer expects warm-cache benefits across requests, we need to commit to a cache warm-up strategy and document the warm state timeline in the checklist.
3) Networking: clarify whether the pilot requires direct peering, private link, or just VPC peering + NAT. Each has different implementation time.
4) Fallbacks: acceptance needs a defined fallback model (hosted fallback, degraded model) if capacity is exhausted.

I can draft an "Arch sign-off" section with exact metrics if we confirm target concurrency.

-rishi
Staff Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision framing: VPC/on-prem acceptance criteria and action lanes

Hannah / team —

I'll pull a rough FTE-weeks estimate and attach it. Two immediate notes:

- For a staged pilot in a single US region (no air-gapped), I estimate ~6-8 FTE-weeks across infra (2 engineers), integration PM (0.5), SRE (1), and security (0.5) to get to a minimally supported pilot. If we do an on-prem appliance/air-gap, multiply by 2-3x due to packaging and on-site validation.
- Cost drivers: networking setup (peering/private endpoint), KMS/HSM integration (if BlueHarbor requires customer-managed keys), and CA-signed certificates for internal endpoints.

I've attached a quick spreadsheet with a line-item for the above (cost-estimate-rough.xlsx).

Attachment: cost-estimate-rough.xlsx (see 'pilot-estimate' tab for breakdown)

Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: procurement@blueharbor.com <procurement@blueharbor.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 31 May 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision framing: VPC/on-prem acceptance criteria and action lanes

Hannah / team —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and attachments. Clarifications from our side: 

- Timeline: BlueHarbor is still targeting an initial pilot sign-off window in Q3; realistically they want a pilot start week of Aug 14 — so we have ~11 weeks to align on scope and staff.
- Data residency: audit logs must be accessible to us in a read-only S3 bucket in our tenancy; logs cannot be co-mingled with other Redwood customers.
- Evidence: SOC2 type II report is required; if you can provide a SOC2 summary + a light network diagram in the first pass that helps our security team.
- Commercial gating: we can agree to a staged commercial commitment — pilot goes on a short-term consumption plan, and a separate Reserved Capacity contract is executed only if pilot meets acceptance criteria within 60 days.

Action for Redwood: please confirm (1) whether you can provide a read-only S3 log export and (2) an initial SOC2 summary and network diagram this week for our security review.

Cheers,
BlueHarbor Procurement (on behalf of BlueHarbor Health)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, procurement@blueharbor.com

Subject: Re: Decision framing: VPC/on-prem acceptance criteria and action lanes

BlueHarbor + team —

Thanks — captured. Proposed action lanes and owners below (quick, so we can iterate):

1) Security evidence (owner: priyom_das) — deliver SOC2 summary + network diagram + KMS approach by Fri, 6/2. Prio: SOC2 summary + network diagram.
2) Arch metrics & fallback model (owner: rishi_malhotra) — define concurrency target, P99 targets, and fallback semantics by Tue, 6/6. Include an explicit KV-cache warm-up note.
3) Pilot ops & staffing (owner: karthik_iyer) — confirm FTE-weeks estimate and on-call rotation by Tue, 6/6. Attach the cost-estimate-rough.xlsx figures.
4) Commercial gating (owner: hannah_schmitt / lauren_bishop) — propose staged milestone payments and the pilot success criteria for contract language by Wed, 6/7.

I'll create a shared drive folder (link above) and add a simple Jira Epic template for tracking. If BlueHarbor confirms the Aug 14 pilot start, we'll treat these as hard deadlines.

Grace
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

> For a staged pilot in a single US region (no air-gapped), ~6-8 FTE-weeks; on-prem/air-gapped is 2-3x effort.
